title: Turn around a tympanic thermometer: eject the used probe cover without touching it, reload, and dock
instruction: Eject the used amber probe cover into the grey tray without touching it or letting it touch the cradle or the white covers, press one fresh white cover from the rack onto the probe and keep it on, rest the thermometer in its cradle, and let go with both hands clear.
context: Between ear-temperature checks, clinical staff eject the used probe cover without touching it, press a fresh cover from the rack onto the probe, and dock the thermometer. In O*NET 31-1131.00 Nursing Assistants (1,505,900 employees, https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/31-1131.00), workers "Record vital signs, such as temperature, blood pressure, pulse, or respiration rate, as directed by medical or nursing staff." In O*NET 31-9092.00 Medical Assistants (833,900 employees, https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/31-9092.00), workers "Interview patients to obtain medical information and measure their vital signs, weight, and height." and "Clean and sterilize instruments and dispose of contaminated supplies." On the Riester ri-thermo tymPRO 1835 (https://riester.de/products/thermometry/ri-thermo-tympro-tympanic-thermometer), "One handed probe cover ejection button aids in the prevention of cross contamination".
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases on the 110 x 130 cm station bench (x forward, y left), single fixed layout (nothing varies by seed), each part within 2 mm and 2 degrees of its bench outline. At (33.0, -20.0) on the right (-y) side a fixed slate-grey stepped rest (our fixture, 38 mm saddle) holds a Riester ri-thermo tymPRO tympanic thermometer (Art. No. 1835, 15.0 x 4.2 x 5.6 cm, 80 g) level, display up, its angled probe towards +y, with one used amber-tinted probe cover (Art. No. 12640; the tint marks it as used) on the probe 8 mm clear of the bench. Near the midline at (33.0, +1.5) lies our grey polypropylene disposal tray (20.0 x 15.0 x 2.0 cm outside, 2.5 mm walls, 180 g). At (15.0, 0.0) stands Riester's desktop cradle for the thermometer and its covers, an open white trough 17.0 x 5.6 cm with its long side along y, walls 4.4 cm high along its rack and 5.8 cm at its pocket end (+y); on its floor a full Art. 12640 rack of ten fresh white covers in 2 rows of 5 (18.5 mm pitch) fills the -y 9.6 cm, the empty pocket the +y end. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: 0 for good, latched at any step (checked on the trial video), if either hand ever touches the used amber cover, if the used cover touches the cradle or any fresh cover, if the ejected used cover touches the bench outside the grey tray, if a fresh cover once on the probe comes off it again, or if the thermometer, cradle, tray or used cover falls off the bench. Otherwise read at the end, with every part of both hands at least 30 mm clear of all task parts, the eject button back within 1.0 mm of rest and every part moving at most 3 mm over 1.0 s (20 steps): 0.5 when the used amber cover rests on the floor inside the grey tray's walls; 1.0 when, as well, one fresh white cover sits on the probe (the probe's tip within 4.0 mm of the cover's axis and 15 degrees of it, at least 9 mm inside) and the thermometer lies in its cradle (within 12 mm of its place along the bench, 6 mm in height and 10 degrees of level, probe towards the pocket end); 0 otherwise. Read on the bench from the trial video and end photos with a ruler.
reset_notes: Under a minute between trials: lift the thermometer out of the cradle, press its eject button over a spare bin to drop the white cover, put a fresh white cover in the emptied rack well so all ten stand, press the amber-marked cover onto the probe until it holds, set the thermometer level on the start rest at (33.0, -20.0) with its probe towards +y, and realign the tray at (33.0, +1.5) and the cradle at (15.0, 0.0) on their outlines.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in 240 Hz PhysX; no write_pose or set_joint in task, scene or demo code. The eject button is a 900 N/m sprung slide (5.5 mm stroke): at 4.0 mm the used cover's weld is cut and it slides off the probe. A cover seats when the probe's 14.0 mm ring presses its 13.8 mm mouth coaxially with 3.5 N; the rim's grip on the ring is a weld made at that pose. Covers weigh 4 g (real: under 1 g); probe and covers are cylinders and square sleeves.
